question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026) CFO Kress explicitly said gross margin will bottom at 71%-72% in fiscal Q4 FY27 due to memory prices, recovering to 72-73% in FY28. Nvidia's habit is point ±50bp guidance, and GAAP = non-GAAP GM recently (75.0/75.0 in Q2; 74.0 guide for both in Q3), so the modal outcome is a 71.5% GAAP midpoint. Slight downside skew: memory costs kept rising and $279B supply commitments are memory-heavy, so 71.0 is somewhat more likely than 72.0; upside from conservatism/pricing actions. Market check: Polymarket only has Q3 ACTUAL non-GAAP GM bins (73-75% ~85%), not Q4 guidance, so it's a near-miss contract used as weak evidence that Q3 is on track; no market found for the Q4 guide itself.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 (reported Aug 26, 2026): revenue $96.2B; GAAP GM 75.0%, non-GAAP GM 75.0% (Nvidia PR).
- Q3 FY27 outlook (same PR): revenue $108.0B ±2%; GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% ±50bp; GAAP opex ~$9.2B.
- Q2 call (Aug 26, 2026; Yahoo/CNBC/Fool Oct 10): CFO Kress said GM to 'bottom in the 71% to 72% range' in fiscal Q4 FY27, partly due to memory prices rising more than expected; FY28 GM to 'settle at 72% to 73%'. Earlier FY27 goal had been 'mid-70s'.
- 10-Q (Jul 26, 2026): $279B long-term supply/capacity agreements, mostly memory (cryptobriefing preview).
- Vera Rubin in production, described as fastest ramp in Nvidia history (call highlights); new-product ramps historically pressure GM early.
- Nvidia guidance format: point ±50bp; GAAP and non-GAAP GM recently guided identical.
- Fiscal 2028 price increases are planned to offset memory costs (search summary of commentary).
- Status quo: Q4 guide consistent with the verbal 71-72% range given in August.
- Polymarket lists bins only for Q3 actual non-GAAP GM (not the Q4 guide).
- Resolves off the GAAP GM midpoint in the Outlook section of the Q3 FY27 press release (expected Nov 17, 2026), rounded to 0.1pp; not off non-GAAP, call commentary, or actual results.
- Event window: a single release, expected 2026-11-17; as of 2026-11-02 the release has not occurred.
- Searched for but not found: any intra-quarter Nvidia update to Q4 margin commentary (Sep-Oct 2026), or consensus estimates for the Q4 GM guide.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs cite the same facts: the CFO's Aug 26 statement that Q4 FY27 GM bottoms at 71-72%, the Q3 guide of 74.0% +/-50bp with GAAP equal to non-GAAP, and the jump in supply commitments to $279B, mostly memory. There was no factual dispute to settle, and I had no web access to check further. The only differences are judgment calls about tail skew: a slight downside lean from memory costs, and whether GAAP could print 0.1-0.3pt below non-GAAP. I agree with the downside lean, and the GAAP gap risk is small given the matched Q3 guide. I carry forward the runs' reference class and 1.2pt dispersion because the evidence supports them.
